name: cost rule: no zero-match stop
why: A page that matched nothing no longer ends browsing, so a 300-entity catalogue is paged through for rows it does not contain.

name: cost rule: no page-count stop
why: A 5 000-release catalogue is paged on although 3 lookups would answer the remaining rows.

name: cost rule: a single pending row is browsed
why: Promotion's lone row at render issues a browse page instead of one lookup, which can only tie at best.

name: inc: hard-coded url-rels (gap)
why: KNOWN GAP: the spec only exercises the release mapping, whose lookup inc set IS url-rels alone, so it cannot see a hard-coded url-rels that would drop release-group-rels/label-rels/artist-rels on the other mappings. Recorded, not hidden.
grep: fetches it in ONE browse request

name: cache: browse page not written to IndexedDB
why: A fresh page in the same context finds nothing under the lookup key and has to fetch again.

name: cache: browse answers not put in L1 (overlap)
why: KNOWN OVERLAP: on re-expand, Phase 1 reads the same answers back from IndexedDB, so no request is made and the spec cannot see the missing L1 entry. Recorded, not hidden.

name: browse phase ignores L1
why: The browse phase counts L1-answered rows as pending again, so with IndexedDB off a re-expand fetches a whole browse page that memory could have served.
